correctness.rationale: For two noncollinear real columns, diagonalize aa^T−bb^T with one strictly positive and one strictly negative eigenvalue to obtain independent chi-squared sums; their ratio is beta-distributed. Apply the exact projection-error height formulas h/alpha and h/beta and the determinant identity h/Lambda for the SVD optimum. The symmetric-beta lower tail decreases for s≥2, giving p_s≤beta/(alpha+beta) and hence E_s≤2h/(alpha+beta)≤2E_*. An equal-norm near-collinear family attains supremum 2 for every s, while a one-row orthogonal small-norm family diverges at inverse square-root rate. Numeric and rational checker supports but does not replace the proof; all boundaries checked.

value.rationale: Determines the minimum number of Gaussian sketch rows needed for any uniform rank-one expected squared-error relative guarantee, a directly motivated parameter of the established sketch-first pivot mechanism, with a sharp universal constant and exact arbitrary-correlation failure law. Explains distinct extremizers: orthogonal ill-conditioned inputs destroy one-row robustness, while equal-norm near-collinear inputs saturate the two-factor even with many rows. This identifies an algorithm-design tradeoff not obtained from general chi-square concentration alone.
